name: Aleks Berditchevskaia
affiliation: Centre for Collective Intelligence Design, Nesta
title: Principal Researcher
about: Aleks Berditchevskaia is the Principal Researcher at Nesta’s Centre for Collective Intelligence Design.  She is the lead author of the report, ‘The Future of Minds & Machines’, on combining human and machine intelligence for problem solving. She is also a co-author of the ‘Playbook for Collective Intelligence Design’, a toolkit for creating projects that mobilise collective intelligence, which has been used to train over 370 staff as part of the UNDP's Accelerator Lab network. In 2019, she designed and ran Nesta's Crowd Forecasting challenge in partnership with BBC Future and the Good Judgement Project.   She holds a PhD in Neuroscience from Imperial College London. Prior to Nesta, Aleks worked in science policy, covering a range of topics from the role of citizen science in research and innovation to the societal implications of machine learning.

name: Róbert Bjarnason
title: Co-Founder and President
about: Róbert, an innovative entrepreneur, founded the first internet companies in Iceland (1993) and Denmark (1995). He co-founded the Citizens Foundation in 2008 to improve public decision making with civic tech. Earlier, he worked in the gaming industry, earning two BAFTAs. He also developed Agent Ruby, an early AI chatbot for artist Lynn Hershman’s, now part of SFMOMA’s digital collection. Currently, he’s developing the Policy Synth project with GovLab, integrating AI and collective intelligence to improve policy-making.

name: Alisson Bruno
title: e-Citizenship Coordinator
about: Alisson Bruno is the Coordinator of the Federal Senate’s e-Cidadania Program, a position he has held since 2015. He holds a Master’s degree in Legislative Power from the Chamber of Deputies and a postgraduate degree in Constitutional Law and Strategic Digital Media Management. With a professional background in public communication and digital engagement, he previously worked in social media management at the Superior Court of Justice. His work focuses on strengthening democratic participation and transparency through digital tools and innovation in the legislative process.

name: Dino Cantú-Pedraza
title: Founder and Director
about: I am currently the Founder and Director of Aceleradora de Ciudades, a national platform working with mayors across Mexico to deliver complex public-space and civic projects within short political cycles. Previously, I served as Secretary of Innovation and Public Engagement in San Pedro Garza García and led national consultation efforts with Mexico’s Supreme Court of Justice.

name: Monica Fonseca
title: Lider Técnico - Gobierno Abierto
about: Through my work at the central IT office in the City of Bogota, I have driven end-to-end digital transformation: from strategy and service design to data, platforms, and operations.  Architectures and interoperability; digital identity and trust (KYC); automation and AI agents in citizen-facing channels (Chatico).  Analytics and executive dashboards (CSAT/NPS, TTR, costs) to support decision-making and continuous improvement; tracking through OKRs, KPIs, and SLAs.  Data governance and responsible adoption: change management, communications, and training for teams and users.  A HumanCity approach to align technology, services, and well-being with clear metrics and full traceability.  Achievement (Sep 2025): Chatico received the 2025 Ibero-American Innovation Award from UCCI, selected among 28 initiatives in recognition of its use of technology to expand equitable access to public services and strengthen citizen participation.

name: Marjan Ehassi
title: Executive Director
about: Dr. Marjan H. Ehsassi is a leading democracy advocate and sought-after expert on citizens' assemblies and their transformative impact on civic engagement. As the Executive Director of FIDE – North America fidemocracy.org/north-america. Ehsassi combines her extensive academic background with practical experience to advance institutional reform. Holding a Doctorate from Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) and a law degree from McGill University, Marjan is the author of Activated Citizenship, The Transformative Power of Citizens' Assemblies (August 2024), which explores how CAs can promote democratic renewal, social cohesion and build mutual trust between elected officials and their constituents. Her book introduces the term "voice insecurity" to spotlight one of the drivers of political grievance. Prior to leading FIDE – North America, she held positions at the World Bank and the National Democratic Institute, where she led governance programs in Asia and the Middle East. She is a member of the OECD Innovative Citizen Participation network and on the Advisory Committee of the Democracy R&D Network. She is a frequent speaker at forums like the Athens Democracy Forum, the American Democracy Summit and has been featured in prestigious publications, including the New York Times, Toronto Star, the Boston Globe. Based in Washington, DC, Dr. Ehsassi is fluent in English, French and Farsi.

name: David Fairman
title: Senior Mediator
about: David Fairman is Senior Mediator at the Consensus Building Institute and Associate Director of the MIT-Harvard Public Disputes Program. For 34 years, he has built consensus and enhanced collaboration capacity on complex public and organizational issues internationally and in the U.S. His primary focus is improving economic and social opportunity and inclusion. He also works extensively on environmental sustainability. His work has been profiled in The New York Times (in 2018 and 2023) and The Washington Post.

name: Eyal Feder-Levy
title: CEO and Co-founder
about: An urban innovator with a passion for cities, future technology, social change and areas in which they converge.   CEO & co-founder of ZenCity, urban startup from Tel Aviv collecting and analyzing wide-scale citizen feedback in cities using advanced AI.   Urban Planner and Web Developer by profession, experienced public speaker and an average guitar player. Curious and fast learner with an entrepreneurial spirit.  Former member of the World Economic Forum Future of Cities advisory board.  Former COO and founding member of Tel-Aviv University's City Center, an interdisciplinary research center for 21st century urbanism.   Youngest board member of the Israeli Urban Planning association.

name: Cristiano Ferri
title: Legislative Official
about: Dr. Cristiano Ferri is the founder and former head of the Hacker Laboratory at the Brazilian House of Representatives, where he also developed and managed the legislative e-Democracy Program. Dr. Ferri is a Research Affiliate at the MIT Center for Collective Intelligence, and has also conducted cutting-edge innovation research at the Leibniz Institute for Media Research and the Ash Center for Democratic Governance and Innovation at the Harvard Kennedy School.

name: Franziska Führer
title: Consultant
about: Franziska is a consultant in the CIO’s office at the City of Vienna. She is an experienced managing director and head of project, communicator, strategist and innovator with a love for troubleshooting.

name: Beth Goldberg
title: Head of Research & Development
about: Beth Goldberg is the Head of Research & Design at Jigsaw, a Google incubator that builds human agency with technology. She leads an interdisciplinary team of researchers and designers who co-design cutting-edge technologies for the hardest civic challenges alongside academics, civil society, and technologists. Beth is also a Senior Fellow and Lecturer on Manipulation & AI at Yale's Jackson School of Global Affairs.

name: Mario Grubišić
affiliation: Directorate for Communication, European Committee of the Regions
title: Head of Sector – Future Lab
about: Mario Grubišić is the Head of the FutureLAB sector in the Directorate for Communication within the European Committee of the Regions (CoR). As part of his responsibilities, he is in charge of citizen engagement programmes within democratic processes. Before this, he was Team Coordinator for the Climate, Energy and Green Deal sector of the commission for Environment, Climate change and Energy (ENVE). As Team Coordinator, he was in charge of the Green Deal Going Local initiative, that encompasses the various policy areas tied to the European Green Deal within the CoR.

name: Kristin Hansen
title: Executive Director
about: As the Executive Director of Civic Health Project, a nonpartisan grantmaking organization, Kristin is dedicated to accelerating the efforts of practitioners, creatives, and academics who seek to reduce polarization, foster social cohesion, and improve civil discourse in our citizenry, politics, and media.  During Kristin’s tenure, Civic Health Project has awarded more than 70 catalytic field grants, funded the Strengthening Democracy Challenge, launched Bridge Entertainment Labs, launched the Mismatch school-based dialogue platform, co-chaired the Bridging Goals & Measures Working Group, and co-founded the U.S. Citizen Assembly and Deliberation Allies (CADA) forum.   In addition to her role at Civic Health Project, Kristin Serves as a Co-Chair of the More Perfect campaign, a Co-Chair of the global Council on Technology and Social Cohesion, and an advisory board member for Listen First Project, More Perfect Union, and Business for America. She also serves as a frequent lecturer and coach in strategic communications at the Stanford Graduate School of Business.

name: Marci Harris
title: Founder and CEO
about: As founder and CEO of POPVOX.com and the Executive Director of the nonprofit POPVOX Foundation, Marci is passionate about the responsible use of technology to improve government and benefit humanity. She is a lawyer and former Congressional staffer, who worked on the House Ways and Means Committee's Affordable Care Act team. She has held fellowships with Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center for Democracy and the New America Foundation, and taught public policy, government, and civic technology courses at the University of San Francisco, San Jose State University, and the University of California Berkeley.

name: Luukas Ilves
title: Advisor to the Deputy Prime Minister
about: Luukas Ilves has been appointed as Advisor to the Deputy Prime Minister at the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. From 2022 to 2024, he served as the Government Chief Information Officer of Estonia. Prior to joining the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, Luukas was the Head of Strategy at Guardtime, where he led the company’s work with governments, international organizations, and NGOs. His focus included addressing complex challenges and areas of strategic importance such as digital sovereignty, cloud adoption, trustworthy AI, and the response to COVID-19.

name: Eve Klein
title: Senior Advisor for Public Engagement in Science
about: Eve Klein is Senior Advisor for Public Engagement in Science with ASTC. In her role, she leads a portfolio of projects that advance the study and practice of public engagement in science, supporting science engagement organizations working at the intersection of public perceptions, science policy, and engagement with emerging issues like AI.

name: Hiroyuki Kurimoto
title: Founder
about: Born in 1999, I entered the Faculty of Policy Studies at Keio University in 2018. At the same time, I started serving as a director of NPOs and working in the secretariat of a nonpartisan legislative body, I founded Liquitous Inc. in 2020 with the concept of "communication agent between citizens and government". Currently, we are developing the digital citizen participation platform and providing it to local governments over 50 municipalities in Japan, as well as designing, managing, facilitating the citizen participation process in planning and project implementation based on the developed consensus building platform. In 2023, I participated in the founding of C&Y Partners, Inc. as a director, which promotes "Children and Youth's Participation like Opinion Expression" in the policy making process as a consultant agency. I am also an advisor for the "Project for Strengthening Business and Financial Management of Local Governments" by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications of the Japanese government.

name: Claudius Lieven
affiliation: Office for Regional Planning and Urban Development, City of Hamburg
title: Head of the Urban Workshop and Participation Unit
about: Claudius Lieven is a political scientist. After working in urban renewal, he served for several years as the Green Party's spokesperson for urban development in the Hamburg Parliament. In 2008, he joined the city's urban development authority, where he established, among other things, the Integrated Urban Development Framework Program (RISE) and the Urban Workshop. Since 2017, he has also led the Digital Participation System (DIPAS) project, and since 2021, he has also been responsible for the BSW (Berlin Social Welfare) measures within the Connected Urban Twins (CUT) project.

name: Jeffery Marino
affiliation: California Office of Data and Innovation
title: Director
about: As Director of the California Office of Data and Innovation, Jeffery Marino directs Engaged California. A seasoned data journalist and tech leader, my expertise lies at the intersection of advanced analytics and storytelling. He's used his unique talents as a data storyteller to craft winning marketing campaigns, drive innovative communications strategies, inform executives about product performance, and to develop high profile thought leadership programs at multiple successful startups. He uses these skills to better serve Californians by improving statewide digital services with hard work, innovation, and above all else, empathy and kindness.

name: Jose Luis Marti
title: Associate Professor of Philosophy of Law
about: José Luis Martí is Associate Professor of Philosophy of Law at Pompeu Fabra University since 2007. He holds a bachelor's degree in Law (1997) and PhD in Political and Social Sciences (2004) by the same university. He has been University Commissioner for the Planetary Wellbeing Strategic Initiative (2021-2024), and Vice-rector of Innovation of Pompeu Fabra University (2017-2021), Secretary General of the same university (2017). He has been principal investigator of a Recercaixa project on "Democratic culture and new forms of citizen participation" (2013-2016), a co-PI of a research project of the National R&D&I Plan on "Justice, legitimacy and global institutions" (2016-2019), PI of the H2020 research project Reconstructing Democracy in a Time of Crisis (REDEM), and co_PI of an Horizon Europe research project on Innovate and Democratic Spaces for Deliberation and Participation (iDEM: https://idemproject.eu/) that explores the use of AI tools to strengthen the participation of people with cognitive disabilities in deliberative processes. He is co-editor of the journal Law, Ethics and Philosophy (LEAP). He has been Laurance S. Rockefeller Fellow of the University Center for Human Values at Princeton University (2008-2009) and a visiting professor at the University of Richmond (2014).

name: Suzette Brooks Masters
title: Director, Democracy Innovation
about: Suzette Brooks Masters is a social entrepreneur, philanthropic advisor, thought leader, and strategist in the fields of democracy, futures, and pluralism. She has decades of experience advising foundations, non-profit organisations, policy makers, and corporations, and serving on nonprofit boards of directors. Suzette has received numerous awards for her philanthropic vision and impact, and accolades for her incisive publications. She prides herself on seeing around corners and challenging conventional thinking.  Suzette currently leads the Better Futures Project at the Democracy Funders Network, a cross-ideological learning and action community for donors concerned about American democracy. She previously served as Senior Strategist at the Center for Inclusion and Belonging at the American Immigration Council, and as Program Director for Migration at the J.M. Kaplan Fund in New York City.  The author of Imagining Better Futures for American Democracy, Suzette is a graduate of Harvard Law School, University of Cambridge, and Amherst College. A lifelong New Yorker, she is the daughter and granddaughter of immigrants.

name: Jonathan Moskovic
affiliation: European University Institute    What about Dem
title: Research Lead      Founder
about: Jonathan is an expert in democratic innovation and citizen participation, with over ten years of experience at local, regional, European, and international levels. He is currently working with a wide range of actors : civil society, traditional political institutions (parties, parliaments, and governments), and international organizations. Jonathan's passion lies in rethinking citizen engagement to make it a vital lever for democracy, ensuring every voice matters in shaping the decisions that define our future.  For over more than a decade, he's had the privilege of contributing to the rise of the deliberative wave across the globe—from Australia to Lebanon, Kosovo, and the United States—through political advocacy, training, strategic reflections, and methodological support. One of his proudest achievements is the establishment of deliberative committees in Brussels—a world first that institutionalises the collaboration between randomly selected citizens and parliamentarians. Because addressing today’s political challenges requires the inclusion of citizens, Jonathan dedicates himself to supporting those who seek to open their institutions to these key actors—who are too often passive spectators in decision-making processes.

name: Geoff Mulgan
title: Professor of Collective Intelligence, Public Policy and Social Innovation
about: I'm an academic, writer, sometime bureaucrat, CEO and social entrepreneur, curious about how the world works and how to improve it. Most of my work has focused on how to solve collective problems.  That has led me both to big ideas, imagination and vision, and to the challenges of practical implementation: connecting the why, the what and the how.  I’ve been lucky to have worked on change from many angles: top-down in governments (in the UK, Australia and the European Commission, and as an adviser to dozens of other governments); bottom-up helping to foster social innovations, start-ups, new organisations and community projects;  in between, running two foundations and several investment funds; and working as an academic, now at UCL.

name: Aline Muylaert
title: Co-Founder & Head of Government Success
about: Impact entrepreneur, recognized as Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe leader, and Co-Founder of Go Vocal.   Go Vocal is a community engagement platform used by +500 cities and governments to reach out to more citizens, set up and manage efficient participation, and drive better policy decisions. We aim to build stronger democracies by making public decision-making more inclusive, participatory, and responsive.

name: Ruthie Nachmany
title: Chief Innovation and Modernization Officer
about: Ruthie Nachmany is a product manager that leads the platform team at the New Jersey Innovation Authority, where she has driven measurable improvements in benefits delivery for over 1 million residents. Her team develops the AI Assistant (the GenAI tool used by the state’s public professionals) as well as other scalable infrastructure that expands New Jersey’s capacity to serve residents. Previously, Ruthie was a product manager on the Resident Experience Initiative focused on supporting New Jersey residents who received unemployment insurance, driving some of the first uses of genAI in the state to support better communications, feedback analysis, and case management.

name: Tarik Nesh-Nash
title: Senior Regional Coordinator, Africa and the Middle East
about: Tarik Nesh-Nash joined OGP in June 2021 as a Senior Regional Coordinator of Africa and the Middle East. He brings diverse backgrounds in technology, law, business, and humanitarian fields with 20+ years of international field experience applied in more than 30 countries in the transparency and citizen participation space.   He has been actively engaged in efforts related to participatory legislation, civic crowdsourcing, data-driven decision-making and open innovation for development.   He has launched a series of social organizations to promote inclusive participatory development including the Center of Excellence for Development, Impact For Development, ICT4Dev Research Center, and GovRight.

name: Evelien Nieuwenburg
title: Co-Founder & Innovation Scientist
about: Evelien is an innovation scientist with a passion for community building and a knack for bringing people together. She is a community organizer and Co-Founder & Innovation Scientist at Dembrane and serves as Vice President of the Association Civic Tech Europe. Dembrane builds AI powered tools to radically improve how organisations listen to their stakeholders at any scale.

name: Alex Parsons
title: Democracy Lead and Senior Researcher
about: Alex is the democracy lead and senior researcher at mySociety. Within the democracy programme, he is responsible for coordinating the team and setting the direction of our democracy work. With his researcher hat, he works across full range of mySociety’s climate, transparency, community, and democracy programmes.  He has a combination political science (MSc in Democracy and Democratization) and technical background – leading on mySociety’s data science work.  His work has included looking at the state of FOI regulation across Europe,  investigating we can improve FOI legislation in the UK, creating new datasets of deprivation in the UK, discovering how local councillors feel about citizens’ assemblies, and digging through the history of people being annoyed by dog poo. He leads on mySociety’s response to consultations, and plays a role in shaping our future programme of work.

name: Lex Paulson
title: Director
about: Lex Paulson is director of the School of Collective Intelligence at the Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique, known as UM6P, in Ben Guerir, Morocco, and a lecturer in human rights at Sciences Po, Paris. Trained as a community organizer, he helped craft mobilization and training strategies for the presidential campaigns of Barack Obama in 2008 and Emmanuel Macron in 2017.

name: Tiago Carneiro Peixoto
title: Senior Public Sector Specialist - Digital Government Coordinator for the EU and Western Balkans
about: Tiago C. Peixoto is a Senior Digital Specialist and the World Bank’s focal point on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Services for the Western Balkans and Europe. Since joining the institution in 2010, he has worked with governments to design and implement digital solutions that improve public policies and service delivery.  Before joining the World Bank, Tiago managed projects and consulted for several organizations, including the European Commission, the OECD, and the United Nations. He has been recognized as one of the 20 Most Innovative People in Democracy and one of the 100 Most Influential People in Digital Government. He is also a recipient of the Louis Brownlow Award from the American Society for Public Administration.  His work has been featured in both mainstream and specialized media, and he has published in leading academic journals, including the British Journal of Political Science, Public Administration Review, Journal of Information Technology and Politics, and UCLA Law Review. Tiago holds a Ph.D. and an M.A. in Political and Social Sciences from the European University Institute, as well as an M.A. in Sociology of Organisations from Sciences-Po Paris.

name: Javier Pérez
title: Director
about: I am the Director of Political Watch, a think-and-do tank specialized in the development of civic technologies to promote transparency, citizen participation, and accountability, and to facilitate informed public debate on the major collective challenges of our time. I studied Economics and Law at Carlos III University of Madrid. Before founding Political Watch, I was the Research Coordinator for trade, agriculture, and climate change at Oxfam International. I have experience in international institutions (the Directorate-General for Development of the European Commission) and in international negotiations (the WTO Summit in Geneva). I am an expert in policy coherence for development, international trade, social movements, and civic technologies. Since November 2025 I've been an Ashoka fellow.

name: Ben Peterson
title: Executive Director of the City-County Planning Commission
about: I am currently the Executive Director of the City-County Planning Commission of Warren County, KY responsible for the operations and oversight of all planning, zoning, GIS, and development for Warren County, KY and the Cities of Bowling Green, Oakland, Plum Springs, Smith’s Grove and Woodburn. Leadership responsibilities and administrative duties include supervision of a fifteen member staff, a two million dollar budget including the Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO), community GIS, and numerous other boards and advisory groups.  Previously, I  held the title of GIS/Planner with the City of Paducah, KY being responsible for managing and maintaining the 6-member McCracken and Paducah GIS Consortium system. Other responsibilities have included a variety of duties including simple cartography, data creation & analysis, server maintenance, creating web-based map services, and management. Prior to this position, I was responsible for all aspects of short and long-range Planning & Zoning, Community Development, and Special Projects.

name: Ricardo Poppi
title: Technology Coordinator
about: Ricardo Poppi is a technology leader who bridges policy and software to advance digital democracy in Brazil. Since 2016 he has coordinated technology initiatives at Instituto Cidade Democrática, steering platforms and algorithms that enable citizen participation in public policies. He also advises the public sector on digital transformation at the Inter-American Development Bank and previously consulted with the United Nations University on e-Participation, reflecting strong international collaboration. With a background in electronics and political science from the University of Brasília (Bachelor and Master), he combines hands-on technical insight with governance, policy design, and democratic reform. Based in Brasília, his work uniquely blends systems thinking, public administration, and open participation to modernize government processes.

name: Raphael Pouyé
title: Policy Analyst
about: Raphael Pouyé is a political analyst and policy expert in democratic innovations and digital governance. He teaches "Open Government and Citizen Participation in the Age of AI" at Sciences Po Paris. He previously led strategic democracy support assignments at the French Development Agency and served as Country Director France for Democratic Society, focusing on public innovation and participatory climate governance. His previous role as Democracy and Innovation Expert with the European Commission included advising 35 EU Delegations and launching the first EU global civic tech contest.

name: Giulio Quaggiotto
affiliation: Prime Minister’s Office, United Arab Emirates
title: Strategic Advisor
about: Giulio is a strategic advisor to the Prime Minister’s Office. As Head of UNDP’s Regional Innovation Center for the Asia Pacific, he worked with governments across the region to develop renewal capabilities and accelerate impact on complex development challenges. He was an MIT Research Associate with a focus on lead user innovation. Prior to joining UNDP, he was the Director of Community at Climate KIC and an Innovation Advisor for the Prime Minister’s Office in the UAE. Giulio’s career includes stints at Nesta, WWF and the World Bank. He was also the manager of the Jakarta Lab of the UN Global Pulse, a flagship innovation initiative of the United Nations Secretary-General on big data for public policy. His interests include portfolio approaches to innovation and incorporating grassroots innovations into national innovation systems. He is a regular speaker at international conferences on the intersection of social innovation, technology and international development.

name: Greta Ríos
title: Co-Executive Director
about: Greta leads People Powered’s work to grow the collective power of organizations and advocates supporting participatory democracy.  She previously served as founder and executive director of Ollin, a Mexican NGO that originally focused on inclusion of youth in the governance of Mexico, and then evolved to take on a broader mission of working toward a country with strong institutions, citizens and democracy. At Ollin, Greta activated thousands of young people to participate in their communities and democracy; supported innovative, large-scale participatory budgeting (PB) programs in several Mexican cities; and coordinated research and monitoring to hold government accountable. In 2019, Greta led and won a legal suit challenging a modification to the Mexico City Citizen Participation Law, which resulted in a new law being enacted.

name: Matt Ryan
title: Senior Fellow
about: Matt Ryan is a researcher and advocate for democratic innovation, citizen participation and evidence-based policy making, with a track record of impactful contributions across local and global spheres.   His research has earned recognition that includes a Chancellor’s Letter of Commendation, The Bill Brugger Prize and a first-class Honours degree from Flinders University and a PhD Research Impact Award at the University of South Australia.  As Deputy Chief of Staff to a South Australian Premier, Matt led a pioneering program of democratic innovation experiments, including major citizens' juries and participatory budgeting projects, which garnered international acclaim.  In his role as Senior Fellow at The Governance Lab (USA), Matt has prepared international reports and developed courses that support public servants worldwide to adopt innovative and participatory problem-solving techniques.  Beyond his academic and professional endeavours, Matt is actively engaged in community activities, fostering collaborations and driving democratic movements in Australia and beyond.

name: Paula Starr
title: Chief Information Officer
about: Paula Starr is a Cherokee citizen leading technology delivery at the Cherokee Nation, the United States’ largest federally-recognized tribe. She leads an IT department that supports 5,000 employees across the 7,000 square mile Cherokee reservation and service delivery to 460,000 citizens across the United States and the globe. Paula’s team takes pride in upholding Cherokee community values while striving to provide protected and reliable services that their co-workers love and enhancing service delivery to help Cherokee citizens live better.   Paula’s professional journey has taken her from starting her career as the first female member of Cherokee Nation’s Hospitality and Gaming IT department to the leadership of private sector technology teams across multiple countries and back to her roots at the Cherokee Nation. Paula has been recognized as one of the Top 100 Women in Technology by Technology Magazine and is the recipient of a Top 50 Technologist OnCon Icon award.

name: Silke Toenshoff
title: Head of Unit
about: Experienced Head Of Unit with a demonstrated history of working in the International Affairs. Skilled in Public Diplomacy and Policy Analysis. A skilled manager of large teams with a Ph.D. in Economics, an MBA in International Management and a Diploma in Arabic from SOAS, University of London and a keen interest in the impact of AI on democracy and politics.

name: Ireland Twiggs
title: Programme Manager
about: I am a programme manager, at Co-operation Ireland, working on the Voice Matters project, which engages with citizens in an AI-enabled deliberative democratic process to develop and implement solutions to community issues. I am passionate about facilitating dialogue and trust between citizens and authorities, and contributing to the repair of entrenched divisions and deep-rooted issues in society.  I have a master's degree in Global Security and Borders from Queen's University Belfast, and a bachelor's degree in Peace and Justice Studies and Religious Studies with a minor in Arabic from Manhattan College where I received multiple awards for my academic excellence and service . I have a strong background in research and field experience, focusing on identity politics and post-conflict reconstruction in South Asia and Northern Ireland. I have also worked in philanthropy and leadership, supporting various organizations and campaigns in the social sector. I am adaptable, diligent, and skilled in active listening, and social awareness. I value community and teamwork, and I am eager to learn and grow in my role.

name: Mark Warren
title: Professor Emeritus of Political Science, Emeritus Merilees Chair for the Study of Democracy
about: Mark E. Warren joined the Department of Political Science University of British Columbia in 2004. As the holder of the Merilees Chair for the Study of Democracy, Warren was charged with establishing the Centre for the Study of Democratic Institutions in the Faculty of Arts, which he directed from 2004-2007. Warren received his B.A. from Lewis and Clark College, and his M.A and Ph.D. from the University of Toronto. He came to UBC from the Department of Government at Georgetown University, where he co-founded the Center for Democracy and the Third Sector. He taught previously at Northwestern University and Rice University.  Warren’s current research interests fall within the field of democratic theory. He is especially interested in new forms of citizen participation, new forms of democratic representation, the relationship between civil society and democratic governance, and the corruption of democratic relationships. He is author of Democracy and Association (Princeton University Press, 2001), and editor of Democracy and Trust (Cambridge University Press, 1999). Democracy and Association was the 2003 winner of the Elaine and David Spitz Book Prize for Democracy and Association, awarded by the Conference for the Study of Political Thought, and also received the 2003 Outstanding Book Award from the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations and Voluntary Action (ARNOVA). Warren has published many book chapters in the areas of democratic theory and continental political thought, and has published numerous articles in journals such as the American Political Science Review, the American Journal of Political Science, and Political Theory.  Warren currently directs a SSHRC-funded Partnership project entitled Participedia (www.participedia.net), which uses a web-based platform to collect data about democratic innovation and participatory governance around the world. Participedia is building the data infrastructure for the emerging field of democratic innovations, as well as serve as a resource for governments, democracy practitioners and advocates.

name: Yanina Welp
title: Research Fellow
about: Yanina Welp is Research Fellow at the Albert Hirschman Centre on Democracy. Between 2008 and 2018 she has been principal researcher at the Centre for Democracy Studies and co-director of the Zurich Latin American Centre (2016-2019), both at the University of Zurich. She finished her Habilitation in 2015 at the University of St.Gallen, with the venia legendi in Latin American Studies and she holds two Bachelor degrees in Social Communication and Political Science from the University of Buenos Aires (Argentina), and a PhD in Political and Social Sciences from the Pompeu Fabra University (Spain). She is founder member of Red de Politólogas.  Her research Interests are democracy and democratization, political institutions, comparative politics, protest and social movements, digital technologies and politics, democratic innovations, mechanisms of direct democracy. Welp has published extensively on these topics in academic journals and books. Her last book is The will of the people. Populism and citizens participation in Latin America (De Gruyter 2022).

name: Aziza Umarova
affiliation: Agency for Strategic Development and Reforms, Uzbekistan
title: Head of Delivery Unit
about: Aziza Umarova is a leading practitioner in public sector reform and development, with a focus on Central Asia and Uzbekistan. With academic foundations in economics and political science, she combines more than a decade of international development experience with ongoing government experience, uniquely bridging global best practices and local execution.  She began her career with UNDP, managing governance projects in Uzbekistan and later advising on public sector innovation at the UNDP Global Center for Public Service Excellence in Singapore. She went on to found SmartGov, a boutique consultancy on governance and innovation, which played a role in major reform initiatives, including in transport, aviation and social protection. Through this work, she partnered with UNICEF, the World Bank, GIZ, and the OECD, where she also served as a monitoring expert for the Istanbul Anti-Corruption Action Plan.  Since 2023, Aziza has been leading the Delivery Unit at the Agency for Strategic Reforms under the President of Uzbekistan. In this role, she spearheads innovation by promoting data-driven policy, strengthening monitoring and evaluation of state programs, building open-source GIS tools to enhance public investment, and advancing whole-of-government strategies to improve social sector outcomes. She is also a contributor to global policy research, authoring chapters in the Public Service Evolution in 15 Post-Soviet Countries (Palgrave, 2022) and Public Administration in the New Reality (Palgrave, 2025). She serves on the Steering Group of the Astana Civil Service Hub and is the Co-Chair of the Regional Association on Public Administration.

name: Micah Weinberg
title: Nonresident Scholar
about: Dr. Micah Weinberg is a nonresident scholar at Carnegie California writing on the global relevance of the quality of democracy and public policy in this important subnational polity.  He is also a Senior Strategic Advisor to the Goldman School of Public Policy at the University of California at Berkeley assisting its leadership in advancing their Democracy Policy Initiative.  Most recently he was CEO of California Forward, quintupling its staff and revenue while having a tremendous impact on public policy in this state. This includes central roles in the creation of the $600 million California Jobs First program, a new international model for equitable economic development, the $500 million California Dream for All program, focusing on expanding homeownership, as well as multi-billion-dollar investments in broadband access and wildfire mitigation.

name: Bill Zipse
title: Supervising Forester
about: I currently work with NJ State Forest Service focusing on strategic planning, program management, and natural resource planning and analysis. I am intrigued by the concept of linking natural resource management with machine learning, artificial intelligence, and open source software development.

name: Naiara Goia
title: Managing Director
about:
I am an innovation professional with more than 25 years of experience leading complex strategic projects with international scope across public, private, and civic sectors. With a multidisciplinary background and training, I combine commitment, innovative mindset, strategic thinking, and leadership to create strategies with transformative impact. Over the course of my career, I have launched initiatives, held leadership roles in multiple organisations, promoted innovation strategies for business and social transformation, and remained deeply engaged in both local and international networks and collaborations.

As the Managing Director of Arantzazulab, my work centres on democracy innovation, governance transformation and public innovation, with a particular emphasis on bridging practice and research, embedding values, advancing feminist leadership, and exploring the role of technology. I am passionate about building networks, connecting people and ideas, and facilitating dialogue, and I thrive on creating inclusive, multi-stakeholder approaches that drive systemic change. An experienced communicator, I frequently speak at national and international forums, contribute to media debates, write in edited volumes, and participate in numerous think tanks on the challenges facing the Basque Country. I also collaborate with universities as a lecturer.

name: Antaraa Vasudev
title: Founder and CEO
about: An experimenter in the civic-technology space, Antaraa Vasudev is the Founder of Civis, a non-profit platform which works to enable effective dialogue between Governments and citizens, on draft laws and policies. She has previously worked at the international non-profit Asia Society, where she handled policy-related public education programmes and Track-II dialogues between Ministers in the Union Council of Ministers and Kevin Rudd (Former Prime Minister of Australia). In addition to her work at Asia Society, she volunteered for the global civic-technology platform Democracy. Earth. She started her career understanding how technology can drive civic engagement at Niti Digital. She is driven to help build trust between citizens and government through the use of technology and is a part of Forbes' Asia 30 Under 30 Class of 2021.

name: Alex Fischer
title: Fellow
about: Dr Alex Fischer is an Honorary Research Fellow engaging with the ANU School of Cybernetics’ faculty, research students and Practitioner Network. He brings his interdisciplinary training and global cross-sector experiences to pressing questions about how technology is being designed to accelerate progress across the Sustainable Development Goals. His policy and practice interests include how smart-monitoring technologies are shaping rural drinking water services, how Bayesian analytic approaches are enabling adaptive community and government initiatives aimed at improving intergenerational societal health and how new data flows are changing policy and accountability pathways ranging from community to watershed to national scales. His academic research explores how competing media and policy narratives interact to shape public priorities and how to design polycentric institutions by considering the way information systems link to decisions and performance outcomes.

name: Bonnie Shaw
title: Chief Innovator in Residence
about:
Bonnie Shaw is a leader in public sector innovation and adaptive leadership and has shaped a diverse multidisciplinary career across public, private and social impact sectors and startups. 

Bonnie is the Chief Innovator in Residence at the Municipal Association of Victoria, where she leads the MAVlab - an innovation lab serving all 79 councils in Victoria. She is also a Professor of Practice in the School of Design and Social Context at RMIT University where she is pursuing a program of research focused on the cognitive and behavioural impacts of chronic stress.
